messages:
alex: quick checkin — ran a small sweep on the new sparse-qkv packing + epilogue-rewrite. baseline fused kernel (v2) vs sparse-packed (w/ partial lane skip). results are weird: +8% throughput at seq=64 but -15% at seq=1024. attached numbers below.

alex: bench harness: `./bench_attn --model=gpt-medium --seq=64,256,1024 --heads=16 --batch=1..8 --warm=5 --iters=50`

alex: raw median latencies (ms / token) — fewer decimals for readibility:
- fused-v2: seq64=0.9, seq256=1.7, seq1024=3.9
- sparse-pack: seq64=0.83, seq256=1.72, seq1024=4.5

alex: flame diffs from perf-bot show hot spot in L2 copy + epilogue path when seq>512. seems like the sparse packing reduces compute but increases irregular L2 traffic. :thinking_face:

perf-bot: profile links: https://perf.internal/graphs/2912345678/spf-flame (flame) and https://perf.internal/alloc/2912345678 (alloc table) :mag_right:

jin: good catch. does packed layout change memory stride for KV pages? that would explain L2 thrash.

alex: yeah — packing compresses Q,K,V into contiguous tile frames, but for paged KV the read pattern becomes less predictable: pages get touched out-of-order. for small seq it's great (cache fits); for long seq the working set crosses multiple pages -> extra memcpy in epilogue.

marie: can you paste the kernel launch + shared mem sizes? curious if shared mem/exchange is forcing more global load.

alex: snippet: ```cuda
// simplified
launch(attn_kernel_sparse_pack, grid, block, sm_bytes)
sm_bytes = heads * lane_sz * sizeof(float) * 2 // q/k temp buffer
```

alex: increasing sm_bytes to keep more per-lane state reduced global loads but bumped occupancy so worse perf at seq64. tradeoff.

sam: maybe we need a hybrid chooser: for seq<=128 use sparse-packed fused epilogue; for seq>512 fallback to paged-friendly non-packed path. also factor in batch size and head count.

jin: agree. we should make kernel_chooser consider: seq_len, batch, head_dim, kv_paging_enabled, and last access stride (if available). add a cost-model term for estimated page crosses.

marie: alternative: keep packing but add an on-the-fly reordering that issues coalesced page reads into a staging buffer, then epilogue can operate linear. adds a copy but may reduce random L2. worth microbenching.

alex: I tried a tiny prototype of that: copy stage + reuse buffer. seq1024 latency went from 4.5 -> 3.95, still worse than fused-v2's 3.9. alloc overhead + extra memcpy cost kills for mid seq. but for seq=2048 it helps.

sam: so no one-size-fits-all. can we encode these heuristics into the runtime and auto-profile per model? maybe run a quick calibration at model load: sample seqs and pick preferred kernel variant.

jin: yes — we already have per-model microbench hooks for compilation. extend it to run 3 microbench trials: short, medium, long sequences and record best kernel and fallback. store in model profile.

marie: also flag regressions: we should emit a metric when chosen kernel performs >10% worse than baseline on live traffic for 5m. automatic rollback or forced re-eval.

perf-bot: noted: will add metric hooks `kernel_choice_mismatch` and `kernel_perf_delta` with tags {model, variant, seq_bucket}.

alex: action items from thread:
- jin: prototype chooser that takes seq/batch/head/kv_paged flag + cost model (ETA 2d)
- marie: try the staging-buffer variant at larger seqs, measure mem overhead (ETA 3d)
- sam: add runtime calibration proposal doc + rollback signal (ETA 4d)
- perf-bot: wire up metrics for kernel mismatches (ETA 1d)

jin: I'll push a WIP PR to `eng-runtime/chooser` with a simple cost function: cost = a*page_crosses + b*sm_vs_occupancy + c*compute_cycles. will need help tuning constants.

sam: when you're ready drop the perf traces and I'll add them to release notes. also include config knobs to force a variant for testing.

alex: thanks all. small note — when we do the metric-driven rollback, let's include a canary percentage so we don't flip everyone at once.

marie: +1. also include an integration test that runs bench harness in CI for seq 64/256/1024 to catch regressions early. tiny run but better than nothing.

alex: cool. I'll paste the initial logs and the perf links into the PR. ping me if you want the raw pprof. :thumbsup:
